newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE trades record January volumes.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE trades record January volumes.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Tuesday 17.3 million futures and options contracts had been traded during January, the highest volume ever traded in the first month of the year.
Volumes were up 17 percent on January 1996, the previous January record, when over 14.7 million contracts were traded.

During the month, one month Euromark futures set a daily volume record of 14,665 contracts and three month Eurolira futures set a daily volume record of 88,837 contracts on January 15 and 29 respectively.
New monthly records were set in the one month Euromark and three month Eurolira futures and in the FTSE 100 index option.
Daniel Hodson, LIFFE's chief executive, said this was an excellent start to what could well be LIFFE's most challenging year.

"This volume demonstrates the market's confidence in the Exchange in the run up to economic and monetary union (EMU) and confirms the importance of London as Europe's leading international financial centre," he said. "Uncertainty about EMU is reflected in higher volumes across the product range."
